detail.title: AI Dependency and Reduced Autonomy in Athletes
detail.summary: Evidence indicates that AI training recommendation dependence functions as a serial mediator in reducing athlete training self-efficacy. This occurs through a pathway: dependence on AI recommendations increases body signal outsourcing, which lowers self-regulation, leading to increased decision hesitation and ultimately lower self-efficacy.
detail.reason: Revision incorporates new structural equation modeling results validating the serial association between AI dependence and reduced training self-efficacy.
